title: Paul Gonsalves and Duke's tactics
summary: Paul was great when straight; Duke called Paul's hardest number when he was stoned or sleeping and used Harold Ashby as a replacement.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: No. Well, there's some other guys. Well, tell me about Paul.
Oh, Paul was a great saxophone player. When And Paul was straight, I think he was one of the greatest tenor
saxophone players around.
You do?
Yeah. When he was straight.
Do you feel he did as much in the band as Ben did?
Yeah.
You did.
In his area, yeah.
Yeah. He was more -- something more of a modernist than Ben, wasn't he?
Yeah. He was a great musician, too, Paul.
Yeah.
When you'd catch him straight, he was something else.

Yeah. Just on that subject, because we were going to talk about how Duke did about that, so Duke was pretty canny when guys were pulling something, or when things happened to guys. I mean, when Paul would come on and he would be stoned, or something like that, or he'd be sitting up there sound asleep or something, Duke would throw his number at him, wouldn't he?
That's right. The hardest number Paul had to play, Duke would call.
(Laughter)
Everybody'd be talking about, 'No, Duke, he can't make it.' Duke would go right ahead.
(Laughter)
The fastest he could play it.
(Laughter)
Well, what was Duke's thinking on that? Would he just enjoy that? Or --
I don't know, but that's what he would do every time.

That's what he would do. He would do that to -- well, didn't he also, keeping guys on their toes, didn't he sometimes call a number, say, like, well, say, call a number that was Paul's, and Paul not be on the stand, and somebody else have to fall in there and scuffle with it?
Oh, sometimes he would, yeah.
I mean, that's --
He would have Harold Ashby play it.
Yeah.
Harold Ashby would fall right in and play it.
Yeah. What about Harold Ashby? Did you like him?
Yeah. A wonderful saxophone player.
Yeah.
Not like Paul, though.
